goal: Minimal direct Action status/classification editing and intuitive accessible single/batch containment and sequence manipulation.
authority: User-requested status icons above Title, Project/Tags controls, removed parent/order inputs, list drag reorder/reparent and multi-select drag; subsequent orange Flag instruction relayed by root.
provenance: lib/domain/core.ts Action, orderedActions, action_project/action_tag and edit semantics
legacy_context: Autosave UI already replaces routine Save/Review, preserves exact raw text and unknown request recovery. Parent/order inputs are replaced by direct manipulation; persisted meaning remains containment and sibling sequence.
vs_legacy: Adds explicit classification editing, icon lifecycle control and accessible batch movement; no execution dependencies or inferred membership.

defaults.value: Distinct upper/lower Before/After zones; center Into append; explicit top-level append zone.
defaults.basis: Minimal spatial defaults chosen within delegated UX scope; destination feedback must make them observable.

defaults.value: Canonical full-tree relative order of deduplicated selected roots; never selection click order.
Unavailable across independent Project root groups; use explicit Project control for classification. Into preserves own membership.
Clear the batch selection when changing scope/filter, preserving drafts and any frozen dispatched operation; do not move hidden selections accidentally.
Assign existing Projects/Tags only; catalog CRUD remains outside this request.
Drag begins from dedicated grip after 6 px movement; edge auto-scroll re-evaluates destination. Ordinary row scrolling remains available.

API ids order is explicit caller intent; UI derives IDs from canonical full snapshot order. Only nonempty unique owner-existing IDs and existing 262144-byte envelope bound; no arbitrary 200-action cap.
Only destination sibling groups rerank; source-only remaining siblings keep gaps and mutual order. Effective no-op does not rerank unrelated values.
Grip Space/Enter opens compact Move chooser. Tab/native select arrows choose placement and destination; focused Move button Enter commits; Escape cancels. Same pure intent/effect as pointer/touch.

then: Named icon buttons above Title expose Active, On hold, Completed and Dropped; the current state is discernible visually and through accessible pressed state. Icon-only buttons have English accessible names/tooltips.
A valid state choice saves directly without Save/Review; completion preserves descendant cascade meaning with concise feedback and Undo.
Parent and numeric Order inputs are absent; Title, raw Notes, Due/Defer and direct Flag remain editable.
scenarios.counterexample: An unlabeled decorative icon replaces status, routine review returns, or removing parent/order also removes hierarchy navigation.
scenarios.exit_observation: Parent and numeric Order inputs are absent; Title, raw Notes, Due/Defer and direct Flag remain editable.

scenarios.given: Existing Projects and Tags, including identical names in different paths, are available.
scenarios.when: Assign or clear Project; toggle Tags in detail.
then: One Project or no Project can be chosen, and multiple existing Tags independently selected; full paths disambiguate identical names.
Changes save directly and preserve unedited raw text, lifecycle, dates, Flag and action containment. No implicit descendant membership propagation or catalog creation.
If membership removes the Action from the current filtered list, detail/return route stays reachable and explains actual saved membership minimally.
scenarios.counterexample: Moving an Action under another Action inherits its Project/Tags, clearing Project removes its parent, or tag controls permit only one Tag.
scenarios.entry_observation: Existing Projects and Tags, including identical names in different paths, are available.
scenarios.exit_observation: If membership removes the Action from the current filtered list, detail/return route stays reachable and explains actual saved membership minimally.

scenarios.given: A list has several visible Actions.
scenarios.when: Click a row; Ctrl/Cmd-toggle additional rows; Shift-select a range; use touch selection affordances.
then: Normal row activation opens detail; a small distinct selection affordance toggles membership without triggering completion or dragging.

Ctrl/Cmd toggles individual membership; Shift extends from the last selection anchor across the current visible canonical list, including both endpoints. Hidden/nonmatching Actions are never silently selected.
Selected rows, count and Clear selection are perceptible and keyboard accessible. Touch can form the same set without modifiers or long-press-only discovery.

Changing scope or filters clears live batch selection and drag hover; local drafts and a dispatched frozen move survive. Starting a drag on an unselected row moves only that row; a selected row moves the selected bundle.
scenarios.counterexample: Opening detail unexpectedly starts a batch, Shift includes hidden filtered rows, or touch users cannot select multiple Actions.
scenarios.entry_observation: A list has several visible Actions.
scenarios.exit_observation: Selected rows, count and Clear selection are perceptible and keyboard accessible. Touch can form the same set without modifiers or long-press-only discovery.

scenarios.given: One Action or a selected set can move within a valid sibling group.
scenarios.when: Begin dragging from a distinct grip and hover upper/lower row edges.
then: Before/After insertion lines identify the exact target position; feedback names or distinguishes the destination, number of moving roots and pending operation.
Dropping above/below means sibling placement under the target parent; selected roots preserve their canonical relative order as a contiguous block, and each subtree retains its internal order.
Drop commits one atomic move directly; pointer cancellation/Escape/outside drop commits nothing and leaves meaningful selection/focus.
Source-only sibling groups retain rank gaps and mutual order; only actual destination groups may have ranks normalized. An unchanged effective structure does not produce gratuitous reorder feedback.
scenarios.counterexample: A vague whole-row highlight arbitrarily nests, selected order follows click order, or one drag creates several independently committed writes.
scenarios.entry_observation: One Action or a selected set can move within a valid sibling group.
scenarios.exit_observation: Drop commits one atomic move directly; pointer cancellation/Escape/outside drop commits nothing and leaves meaningful selection/focus.

scenarios.given: A valid destination Action can contain the moving roots.
scenarios.when: Hover its center nesting zone and drop; alternatively choose the explicit top-level drop zone.
then: Center nesting is visually distinct from Before/After, announces Into plus target, and appends roots after all existing destination children while preserving their relative order.
A named top-level zone removes parent containment and appends roots within their existing root Project groups; classification does not change.
Self/descendant/cycle destinations are visibly unavailable; a multi-selection containing the destination cannot create a partial or cyclic move.
Mixed-Project selections may detach atomically: each root appends within its own unchanged Project group, preserving bundle order within that group, without promising a global cross-group block.
scenarios.counterexample: An ambiguous center drop reorders instead of nesting, moving to top-level silently assigns Inbox, or only part of an invalid batch commits.
scenarios.entry_observation: A valid destination Action can contain the moving roots.
scenarios.exit_observation: Self/descendant/cycle destinations are visibly unavailable; a multi-selection containing the destination cannot create a partial or cyclic move.

scenarios.given: Selection contains an ancestor and its descendant plus another independent root.
then: Only selected roots with no selected ancestor move directly; descendants travel exactly once with their ancestor, retaining internal parent links and order.
The moving count distinguishes roots from included descendants; the entire operation remains atomic and Undoable.
All untouched lifecycle, own Due/Defer, direct Flag, Project and Tags are preserved; effective visibility may change through parent Defer and is conveyed when the Action leaves the view.
scenarios.counterexample: A selected child detaches separately from its selected parent, a subtree duplicates, or the move invents dates or copies flags.
scenarios.entry_observation: Selection contains an ancestor and its descendant plus another independent root.
scenarios.exit_observation: All untouched lifecycle, own Due/Defer, direct Flag, Project and Tags are preserved; effective visibility may change through parent Defer and is conveyed when the Action leaves the view.

scenarios.given: The list is filtered and hidden siblings/ancestors exist in the full saved structure.
scenarios.when: Insert before/after a visible sibling or append Into a target.
then: The full authoritative structure determines destination siblings; hidden siblings are retained and their mutual relative order stays unchanged. Before/After is relative to the named target, not an invented adjacent visible-only rank.
Filtered matches remain exact; no nonmatching parent is silently inserted as a matching row. Minimal context exposes destination containment when its parent is hidden.
If a full fresh structure or unambiguous destination cannot be obtained, movement is unavailable with a concise reason rather than guessing.
scenarios.counterexample: Visible-only renumbering loses hidden siblings, filtered rows are treated as one sibling group, or a missing parent becomes null.
scenarios.entry_observation: The list is filtered and hidden siblings/ancestors exist in the full saved structure.
scenarios.exit_observation: If a full fresh structure or unambiguous destination cannot be obtained, movement is unavailable with a concise reason rather than guessing.

scenarios.given: Root Actions belong to different Projects, whose root order is grouped independently.
scenarios.when: Attempt Before/After across incompatible root Project groups.
then: Cross-group sibling Before/After is unavailable with a concise reason because Project membership is independently edited in detail. Into a valid Action remains an explicit containment operation preserving membership.
Root reordering stays inside each existing Project/unassigned group; a mixed selection is not silently made to share a Project.
No gesture implies a Project/Tag assignment not explicitly selected in detail.
Mixed-Project root detach is permitted and appends separately in each preserved Project; root Before/After rejects any effective root whose Project differs from the anchor Project.
scenarios.counterexample: A drop changes project_id to make an otherwise impossible global order appear to work, or promises a cross-group sequence the canonical list cannot show.
scenarios.entry_observation: Root Actions belong to different Projects, whose root order is grouped independently.
scenarios.exit_observation: No gesture implies a Project/Tag assignment not explicitly selected in detail.

scenarios.given: An Action has unsaved text or membership edits and a move is pending.
scenarios.when: Continue typing; navigate; receive refresh/host updates.
then: Local drafts remain bound to their original Action; IME text/caret survives focus changes and updates. Moves and autosaves serialize without silently overwriting one another.
A moved/filtered-out selected Action and any dirty proposal remain reachable through a named minimal return path; selection refers to stable IDs rather than row positions.
Structural changes during hover invalidate stale feedback; a definite overlapping change requires renewed destination choice rather than silently rebasing the old move.

Movement waits for valid prior autosaves/classification proposals and IME completion; invalid/conflicted drafts visibly block rather than disappearing. Classification acknowledgments clear only submitted Project/Tag versions, leaving newer proposals intact.
scenarios.counterexample: A timer edits the new row, a reordered selection jumps to different IDs, or concurrent moves overwrite an externally changed parent/order.
scenarios.entry_observation: An Action has unsaved text or membership edits and a move is pending.
scenarios.exit_observation: Structural changes during hover invalidate stale feedback; a definite overlapping change requires renewed destination choice rather than silently rebasing the old move.

scenarios.given: A batch move has an unknown result or a definite rejection.
scenarios.when: Check result, retry, refresh or Undo after a confirmed move.
then: Unknown retains the exact original operation ID and arguments; Check result/Retry remain reachable, and identical replay never duplicates the move. No fresh-ID replay or automatic retry storm.
Definite failure preserves saved structure and local drafts/selection with concise feedback; the batch never appears partially saved.
One Undo restores all affected structural changes atomically when safe; later conflicting edits are not overwritten without explicit resolution.
scenarios.counterexample: Each selected root has separate recovery/Undo, unknown is treated as failure, or later corrections are reverted by old replay.
scenarios.entry_observation: A batch move has an unknown result or a definite rejection.
scenarios.exit_observation: One Undo restores all affected structural changes atomically when safe; later conflicting edits are not overwritten without explicit resolution.

scenarios.given: The UI is narrow/full and operated by mouse, touch, keyboard or assistive technology.
scenarios.when: Select, move, nest, cancel and recover.
then: Pointer dragging works on touch with a distinct grip, movement threshold and edge auto-scroll; ordinary scrolling and text editing do not initiate dragging. HTML desktop drag events alone are insufficient.

A compact selection action exposes an equivalent keyboard/touch Move operation with named Before/After/Into/top-level choices; destination selection performs the same direct atomic move without a generic Save/Review screen.
Targets/status feedback are readable without color alone; focus follows stable selected/target identity, scrolling reveals active destination, and no horizontal overflow hides controls.

The dedicated pointer grip uses a 6 px start threshold. Keyboard grip Space/Enter opens the compact Move chooser; Tab and native Arrow navigation choose placement/destination; Enter on the Move button commits, Escape cancels. Pointer/touch and chooser use identical validated movement intent and atomic effect.
scenarios.counterexample: Touch cannot drag, keyboard users must edit removed parent/order inputs, or an invisible offscreen drop zone is required.
scenarios.entry_observation: The UI is narrow/full and operated by mouse, touch, keyboard or assistive technology.
scenarios.exit_observation: Targets/status feedback are readable without color alone; focus follows stable selected/target identity, scrolling reveals active destination, and no horizontal overflow hides controls.

scenarios.given: Flag controls and status icons are visible in light/dark modes.
scenarios.when: Toggle Flag and inspect both states.
then: Flagged icons/toggles use an orange-family active color; unflagged controls are neutral. Direct boolean state remains independently accessible via name and pressed/checked state.
Orange Flag treatment is distinct from lifecycle selection accent and has legible contrast in both themes; it is never the sole indication of state.
Flag changes preserve status, dates, containment and classification.
scenarios.counterexample: Flag remains blue, orange is used for every selected status, or a color-only flag loses its accessible meaning.
scenarios.entry_observation: Flag controls and status icons are visible in light/dark modes.
scenarios.exit_observation: Flag changes preserve status, dates, containment and classification.

required_browser_scenarios: Mouse single and batch Before/After/Into/root with ancestor+descendant selection; cancel and cycle invalid feedback.
320/390px touch grip drag with scrolling, edge auto-scroll and equivalent selection+Move; keyboard full flow with meaningful focus and accessible names.
Filtered hidden sibling/parent and cross-Project root-group fixture; verify no inferred membership and no loss/duplication.
Delayed move response while typing, host refresh, late IME; missing response exact Check/Retry and atomic Undo/conflict.
Project/Tags reassignment removing current match; return route; status icons above Title; orange Flag in light/dark; no parent/order/Save/Review.
validation_gates: Pure deterministic selection/drop planning/normalization with no input mutation.
Real store shared contract: atomic multi-root parent/order updates, CAS, receipt/replay, Undo and owner isolation; a passing mock cannot establish D1 atomicity.
Complete authoritative snapshot planning preserves hidden siblings and canonical root groups.
pnpm check/build and built-resource tests; no failed/skipped/unexecuted acceptance represented as pass.
Actual ChatGPT Work host/cache/auth evidence remains distinct from local browser/mock proof.
technical_handoff: The observed current edit operation updates one Action. A safe batch write/receipt/Undo contract requires boundary design; do not implement batch as multiple ordinary edit commits.
Numeric rank strategy and affected sibling rewrite footprint are design choices, provided visible sequence and atomicity satisfy these contracts.
scope_limits: No catalog CRUD, dependency edges, planned dates, new management method, recommendations, deployment or remote data reset.
No routine confirmation or explanatory paragraphs; concise exceptional destination/error/cascade/recovery meaning remains accessible.
status: Candidate acceptance contract; no implementation acceptance or kernel claim.

adopted: Mixed-Project root detach allowed atomically, appended per unchanged Project group.
Root anchor Before/After rejects Project mismatch.
API supplied IDs preserve caller order; UI supplies canonical tree order.
Existing 262144-byte bound, nonempty unique owner IDs; no arbitrary count cap.
Source-only rank gaps preserved; destination-only rerank; selection clear on scope/filter with drafts/frozen operation retained.
6 px dedicated-grip pointer threshold, edge auto-scroll and equivalent keyboard/compact Move.
Root explicitly adopts compact Move chooser as keyboard equivalent; no independent Arrow drag mode required.
Four direct named lifecycle icon buttons above Title are the adopted one-click status control, replacing an earlier single-button popup alternative.
reconciliation.design_wording_correction: Design ui.selection describes optional shift range. DRAG-03 requires desktop Ctrl/Cmd toggle and Shift range as delegated; do not omit Shift in implementation.
reconciliation.approval_limits: Native artifact reconciliation only; independent design acceptance and implementation validation remain separate.
